capabilities: Pin open parent folders at the top of the file explorer while scrolling
Merge nesting levels deeper than the row limit into one shared row
Highlight a folder's whole range when hovering its indent guide, pinned row or grey name
Collapse folders by clicking pinned rows, grey names or indent guides
Open Obsidian's folder context menu from a pinned row
disambiguation: Not a bookmarking or favorites tool for pinning chosen folders; it only keeps the open parent folders of your current scroll position visible.
extras: Not yet in the community plugin list; the README gives BRAT and manual install steps. Requires Obsidian 1.13 or later and only works with the core file explorer, not plugins that replace it. Known limits: dropping files onto pinned rows does nothing, hover hints need a mouse, and internal Obsidian API changes could break it.
intentEvidence: Keep parent folders pinned at the top of Obsidian's file explorer while you scroll
motivation: Vaults organised by date or project get deep fast: Work / Meetings / 2026 / 2026-05 / 2026-05-21 / …
problem: In deeply nested vaults, scrolling the file explorer slides parent folder rows out of view, leaving only indent lines that don't show which folder you are in.

relations.evidence: Inspired by the sticky scroll in Visual Studio Code.

summary: Sticky-scroll headers for the file explorer that keep open parent folders pinned at the top while you scroll deep folder trees.
